blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Bradner Road is the area's north-south road, and Aberdeen Elementary sits on it at 2975 Bradner Road.
Fraser Highway is the area's north edge, and BC Transit's route 21 stops at Fraser Highway at Lefeuvre Road on its run between Aldergrove and Bourquin Exchange.

Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) lies south of the Aberdeen housing area, and the City's airport development guidelines cover the private properties near YXX that sit under the federal Airport Zoning Regulation.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are single-detached homes on rural and agricultural lots, and the agricultural zones set the lot floor: the Agricultural One (A1) zone's minimum subdivision size is 8.0 ha and the Agricultural Two (A2) zone's is 16.0 ha.

The stock is freehold farm and rural-residential land, and the City's AgRefresh work records the agricultural pattern as two designations, Agriculture 1 – Uplands on A1 patterns and Agriculture 2 – Lowlands on A2 patterns.

Rural houses here are privately serviced in the rural pattern, and a City council report describing rural residential development in Abbotsford states that such homes are usually serviced by wells and septic fields, as urban services are not located within the vicinity.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The one-residence rule governs most farm parcels, because land in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence under the Agricultural Land Commission rules.
A principal residence in the ALR is capped in size, and the Commission states it must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less with no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction.

Airport height rules apply on land under the Airport Zoning Regulation (AZR), and the City's guidelines state that no building, structure or object may exceed in elevation any approach surface, outer surface or transitional surface at that location.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Rural water service is capped by bylaw, and the City's Waterworks Regulation Bylaw limits water service connections for properties outside the Urban Development Boundary to a maximum of 25 mm in diameter, and bars their use for open field crop irrigation.

NAV CANADA assessment takes time, and the City's YXX guidelines state that NAV CANADA attempts to respond within 8 to 12 weeks of receiving a complete land use proposal — a tall shop or barn near the airport is not a quick permit.

The Abbotsford School District's own acknowledgement names the Máthxwi First Nation and the Semá:th First Nation as the Nations on whose traditional and unceded territory the district, including Aberdeen Elementary, sits.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Abbotsford's 2026 residential (Class 1) municipal rates are 1.08284 per $1,000 for police and 1.78296 per $1,000 for general and debt servicing under Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026, before regional and library levies.

Farm-class (Class 9) land is taxed on a different municipal schedule in the same bylaw, and a mixed house-and-farm property can carry both classes on one notice, so the class split on the BC Assessment record is part of the cost check.

Where a rural Aberdeen property is on City water, the connection is capped at 25 mm outside the Urban Development Boundary, and metered residential water is $1.46 per cubic metre and sewer $1.35 per cubic metre effective March 1, 2026.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax applies here, because the Province's taxable-areas list names the City of Abbotsford.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: getting around

items.t: Route 21 is the area's bus link, running between Aldergrove and Bourquin Exchange via Highstreet, with stops at Fraser Highway at Lefeuvre Road, Highstreet Exchange and South Fraser Way at Clearbrook Road.
Bradner Road is the local north-south road, carrying Aberdeen Elementary at 2975 Bradner Road and connecting the farm lots to Fraser Highway at the north edge.
Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) is the area's air link, and the City's airport guidelines cover the lands around it under the Airport Zoning Regulation shown on drawing M-500.

blocks.text: Aberdeen Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check whether the lot is inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500 before planning any tall building, because the City will not release a building permit for AZR land until NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are presented.

Confirm ALR status before valuing a second dwelling, because the Commission's one-residence rule and the 90 m² / 186 m² additional-residence caps apply on ALR parcels whether or not the listing mentions them.

Pull the well and septic records for the specific parcel, because a City report describes rural residential homes in Abbotsford as usually privately serviced by wells and septic fields where urban services are not in the vicinity — servicing is a parcel check, not an area assumption.
Check the lot's floodplain status on Schedule "E" of the Zoning Bylaw, because the bylaw's floodproofing areas are mapped and apply by mapped area, not by the Aberdeen name.

blocks.text: Aberdeen home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

29 houses sold in Aberdeen with a median price of $1,335,000 (the middle half sold between $1,262,500 and $1,482,500), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 97.5% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $388 per square foot, a median year built of 2010 and a median lot of 6,487 square feet.
